findings.claim: It includes both self-esteem (how much a person values themselves) and self-worth (their overall sense of who they are and what they are capable of).
findings.truth: The specification presents self-esteem/self-worth together as the value a person places on themselves. The lesson gives self-worth a separate, broader meaning. Either align the content, flashcard and glossary with the specification, or retain a clearly sourced psychological distinction.

findings.claim: The twelve factors affecting self-concept are ...
findings.truth: The specification lists 14 factors, including emotional development and income. The lesson repeatedly says 12, and its grouped list omits those two factors. Correcting the count and all dependent prompts, checks and flashcards requires a coordinated revision.

findings.claim: Disease is ... an objective, clinically identifiable state ... with specific signs and symptoms.
findings.truth: The specification defines disease as a disorder, usually with specific signs or symptoms. It does not make objectivity, clinical identification or both signs and symptoms part of the definition. The error also appears in answer material, flashcards and the glossary, so revise them together or retain the wider definition only with a reliable cited source.

findings.claim: Measure pulse, blood pressure, BMI, peak flow and temperature, then interpret the results.
findings.truth: The prescribed indicators are blood pressure, peak flow, BMI, waist-to-hip ratio, and resting pulse and recovery after exercise; temperature is not in this list.

findings.claim: Public Health England (now the UK Health Security Agency) ... coordinates national health campaigns.
findings.truth: Public Health England's functions moved to several bodies. UKHSA leads health protection and security, while the Office for Health Improvement and Disparities leads the Department of Health and Social Care campaign resource service.
findings.evidence: GOV.UK, Location of Public Health England functions from 1 October 2021; DHSC Campaign Resource Centre

findings.claim: Change4Life ... rebranded to Better Health in 2020.
findings.truth: Change4Life was brought under the Better Health brand in 2021.
findings.evidence: NHS, Healthier Families: About and contact

findings.claim: Dry January ... encourag[es] people to take a month off alcohol to improve their health and raise money for charity.
findings.truth: Alcohol Change UK describes Dry January as a behaviour-change intervention, not a fundraising campaign.
findings.evidence: Alcohol Change UK, The Dry January challenge and its impact on public health and prevention (2026)

findings.claim: Mark schemes ... often carry a source attribution requirement ... The command word 'Describe' on a 2-mark question ... 'Explain' on a 3-mark question ...
findings.truth: The specification states only that Unit 1 has 80 marks and a balance of short and extended answers based on stimulus and applied contexts. It does not set source-attribution credit or fixed 2- and 3-mark command-word formats. The Assessment Guide was not supplied, so these claims cannot be verified.

summary: Six lessons were checked. Four verified factual corrections are supplied; three wider definition or specification issues need coordinated adjudication, and one unsupported assessment-format claim is noted.
